A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StructRTL research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures and tables, support reliable comparison despite substantial additions and reformatting in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining results, area and delay prediction experiments, baseline comparisons and pretraining-task ablations on a 13,200-design dataset.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds original industrial evaluations, architectural ablations, generalization tests, alternative LLM comparisons and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The core architecture, pretraining objectives and distillation procedure remain. However, Eq. 2 replaces adjacency A with (A+A^T)/2 in positional encoding. Appendix M also introduces an optional inference adaptation that partitions designs at register boundaries, sums predicted subcircuit areas and takes the maximum predicted delay.

E1.justification: Section 4.6 adds 102 industrial RTL modules organized into 51 functionally equivalent pairs, extending evaluation to industrial designs and pairwise quality ranking. v2 also names RTLCoder, MGVerilog and generated RTL among dataset sources, but the unchanged 13,200-design count and statistics do not establish that the underlying training corpus changed.

E2.justification: Appendices J–K add substantively revised comparators: all three CodeV models receive textualized CDFGs, and CodeV-QW-7B is additionally evaluated with full fine-tuning. v2 also removes Graph-XGBoost specifically from the distillation comparison in Table 2, while retaining it in Table 1. These changes substantially broaden the tested LLM alternatives.

E3.justification: The original split, metrics and training configurations remain, but v2 introduces several additional protocols: training with 5%, 10% and 20% of labeled data; disjoint functional clusters formed using embeddings and k-means with k=50; training on the smallest 80% of designs; and industrial pairwise ranking. These supplement rather than replace the original evaluation.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's two pretraining-task ablations, v2 tests stratified masking, input versus embedding masking, positional encodings, GNN/Transformer components and edge-sampling sensitivity. It also adds circuit-type breakdowns, functional and size-shift tests, limited-data analysis, LLM adaptation analyses, partitioning experiments and runtime scaling. These address substantially more questions about mechanisms, robustness and applicability.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new runtime averages and per-class accuracies do not introduce uncertainty estimation or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the shared rows of Table 2 retain their numerical values; the Graph-XGBoost distillation results are removed. Numerous new results appear, including industrial area/delay ranking accuracies of 82.35%/88.23%, partitioned accuracies of 78.43%/88.23%, and fully fine-tuned CodeV-QW-7B validation R2 values of 0.2685/0.0923. These are additional conditions and variants, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Eq. 2 substantively revises the Laplacian definition by replacing A with (A+A^T)/2 while retaining the in-degree and out-degree normalization factors. This is a localized mathematical change rather than equivalent notation. The remaining objectives and metric formulas are retained, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution paragraph and conclusion retain the same central claims: CDFG-based self-supervised representations improve RTL area/delay estimation, and post-mapping knowledge distillation further improves performance. The expanded experiments support these existing claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations for rare-operator masking benefits, poorer sequential-circuit performance, differing area/delay generalization, LLM overfitting and partitioning errors. Section 4.5 and Appendix O newly qualify technology-node transfer, memory requirements and scalability. Appendix M explicitly acknowledges that partitioning has not been validated on designs exceeding 100,000 CDFG nodes.

D1.justification: Existing hyperparameters and hardware descriptions remain. v2 additionally discloses frozen LLM backbones, a 30M-parameter model, approximately 40 hours of single-GPU training and a 42 GB training footprint. It expands dataset provenance and replaces the anonymous code/data repository pointer with a named GitHub code link. These are incremental disclosures, not evidence of changed original training settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for RTLCoder, MGVerilog, text embeddings and k-means, while removing CraftRTL and PRIMAL. It also sharpens the distinction between CDFGs, DFGs and ASTs. The central positioning against hand-crafted graph features and token-based LLM representations remains; publication updates to retained references do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: The shared abstract, methodology and conclusion receive limited wording and terminology edits, while the original narrative order remains. v2 introduces numbered sections, lettered appendices, clearer cross-references, acknowledgments and an impact statement. Most expansion consists of new scientific material rather than extensive rewriting of retained content.

P2.justification: v2 adds limited-data, architectural-ablation, partitioning and runtime figures, plus extensive new result tables. v1's coarse-count table and fine-count histogram are combined into Figure 5, and its node-type table becomes Table 12. The conference template changes typography, headers and caption placement, while appendices switch to a full-width layout.

improvement.justification: v1 mainly validates its claims through the original benchmark and two task-removal ablations. v2 substantially strengthens validation with architectural controls, functional and size shifts, additional LLM comparisons and industrial ranking, while making practical limitations explicit. These gains outweigh limited reporting flaws: uncertainty remains unreported, and Appendix N's 52.18 GB peak-memory value conflicts with Figure 9's 51.0 GB label. The improvement comes from stronger scrutiny and clearer applicability boundaries, not higher retained benchmark scores.
